body:
Coordinator rule (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-05, from w-d57f7ec79343). Two observed_terminal tests that landed with w-814b in 7eb731fc spin forever on Windows; the landing gate was a Linux FULL, where they pass. From now on, a landing that adds or changes tests using filesystem or Git fixtures (temp roots, worktree loss, path walking) gets a Windows run of those new tests before landing, even when the FULL runs on Linux. This doesn't replace the standing rule's gate. It's my check when reading condition 3 and gate evidence.

Fixture isolation lesson retained during the 2026-11-09 memory cleanup from termal-window23-2026-10-18 rev9 and its filed bug w-927a571ee633: a test forward starting at a fixed port collided with the running host's SSH tunnel at 47000, producing peer-unavailable failures before the behavior under test. Reserve an OS-assigned loopback listener and retain its owner through setup instead of assuming a fixed port is free. Diagnose the actual resource owner before attributing such a failure to protocol behavior. This historical example makes no claim that the production allocator is still defective and adds no permission to alter live tunnels or run probes.
